title: Unramified at infinity and not geometrically constant implies nonexceptional
statement:
Let $\psi$ be a nontrivial additive character of $k_0$, let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on
$U_0$. Suppose that $\mathcal M$ is unramified at infinity and not
geometrically constant, in the sense of [rem-dl-a1-conventions]. Then
$\mathcal M$ is constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional]. Geometric irreducibility is not
assumed.

proof.text: Put $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $V=\mathcal M_{\bar\eta}$. This is a nonzero finite-dimensional $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-vector space. By [def-wf-fundamental-representation] and [lem-wf-weil-fundamental-representation] it has the Weil representation $\rho:W(U_0,\bar\eta)\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$. The irreducibility convention in [rem-dl-a1-conventions] says precisely that $V$ is irreducible as a Weil representation. By [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence], the geometric group $G=\pi_1(U,\bar\eta)$ is the kernel of the degree map and hence is normal in $W$. All hypotheses apply: a dense open of the affine line is a smooth geometrically connected separated finite-type curve.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: Weil representation and normal geometric subgroup

proof.text: An irreducible representation is semisimple, so [lem-mg-normal-restriction-semisimple] applies to the finite-dimensional representation $V$ and the normal subgroup $G$, without any finiteness condition on $W/G$. Thus $V|_G$ is semisimple. The current definition [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] identifies the geometric irreducible constituents with the Jordan–Hölder constituents of the geometric stalk module. In a finite direct sum of simple modules, each such constituent is isomorphic to one of the simple summands; therefore each geometric constituent embeds into $V|_G$ as a direct summand. This uses no geometric irreducibility of $\mathcal M$.

Fix $a\in k^\times$. Choose a finite subfield $k_1\subset k$ containing $k_0$ and $a$, possible because $k$ is an algebraic closure of a finite field. Apply [lem-a1-artin-schreier-prime-character-comparison] to the nontrivial $\psi$, obtaining $b\in k_0^\times$ and an identification of $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}$ with the prime-degree $\Psi$-character sheaf for $bax$ on $\mathbf A^1_{k_1}$, and also after geometric base change and restriction to $U$. The fixed character $\Psi$ of [def-fd-additive-character] is nontrivial, and $ba\ne0$. Hence [lem-a1-artin-schreier-ramified-infinity], with its parameter equal to $ba$, says the inertia action on this geometric rank-one stalk has exact order $p$; in particular it is nontrivial. This explicitly compares the degree-$q$ current Artin–Schreier definition with the prime-degree presentation in the local ramification statement.

source.place: Proof, case a != 0: ramification of the linear character

proof.text: Use [d-real-boundary] for $U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_{k_0}$ and the missing point $\infty$: its local inertia group maps into $G$. By [rem-dl-a1-conventions], the unramifiedness hypothesis means this group acts trivially on $V$. If the geometric sheaf $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$ for $a\ne0$ were a constituent, step 2 would give an equivariant injection of its stalk into $V$. For an inertia element $h$ and a vector $v$ in that stalk, injectivity and $i(hv)=h i(v)=i(v)$ give $hv=v$. This contradicts step 3. The inertia calculation uses the same local field at infinity: an open restriction changes neither the function field nor the local ring of the fixed compactification at infinity.

source.place: Proof, case a != 0: contradiction with unramifiedness

proof.text:
For $a=0$, the current definition [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] explicitly identifies the excluded constituent with the trivial rank-one sheaf. If it occurred, step 2 would provide a nonzero $G$-fixed vector in $V$. The subspace $V^G$ is $W$-stable: for $w\in W$, $g\in G$, and $v\in V^G$, normality gives $w^{-1}gw\in G$ and
$$g(wv)=w((w^{-1}gw)v)=wv.$$
By the irreducibility of $V$, its nonzero $W$-submodule $V^G$ equals $V$. Thus $G$ acts trivially on all of $V$, which is geometric constancy by [rem-dl-a1-conventions], contradicting the hypothesis. Together with step 4 this excludes every $a\in k$, exactly constituent-nonexceptionality as defined in [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional].

source.place: Proof, case a = 0 and final conclusion

proof_origin.place: Proof; explicit character-cover comparison added for the main-20261015 statement

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\psi$ be a nontrivial additive character of $k_0$, let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on
$U_0$. Suppose that $\mathcal M$ is unramified at infinity and not
geometrically constant, in the sense of [rem-dl-a1-conventions]. Then
$\mathcal M$ is constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional]. Geometric irreducibility is not
assumed.

proof.text:
Let $V=\mathcal M_{\bar\eta}$, let $W=W(U_0,\bar\eta)$ be the Weil group,
and let $G=\pi_1(U,\bar\eta)\triangleleft W$ be the geometric fundamental
group, as in [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. Since $\mathcal M$ is
irreducible, $V$ is a simple $W$-module. By
[lem-mg-normal-restriction-semisimple], $V|_G$ is semisimple. Hence
every geometric irreducible constituent of $\mathcal M$ is a
$G$-stable direct summand of $V$.

*Case $a\ne0$.* Suppose $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$ were a direct
summand of $V|_G$. The inertia group at
$\infty\in\mathbf P^1_k$ maps into $G$. Restricting from
$\mathbf A^1$ to $U$ does not change the local field at $\infty$. The
inertia group acts trivially on $V$ because $\mathcal M$ is unramified
at infinity, so it acts trivially on every summand. But
$\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}$ is ramified at infinity by
[lem-a1-artin-schreier-ramified-infinity]. This is a
contradiction.

*Case $a=0$.* Suppose the trivial rank-one representation were a
geometric constituent. Then, being a direct summand, it gives
$V^G\neq0$. The subspace $V^G$ is $W$-stable because $G$ is normal: for
$w\in W$, $g\in G$ and $v\in V^G$,

$$
g\,(wv)=w\,(w^{-1}gw)\,v=wv .
$$

Since $V$ is a simple $W$-module, $V^G=V$. So $G$ acts trivially and
$\mathcal M$ is geometrically constant, contrary to hypothesis.

So no geometric constituent is of the form $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$
with $a\in k$.

tool_uses.why: Defines the Weil and geometric stalk representations; the unit uses these generic notions.
Provides the representation homomorphism, which its definition alone does not assert; no same-unit lemma does this.
Identifies the geometric group as the degree kernel, needed for normality; no same-unit lemma states the group exact sequence.
The unit explicitly calls for normal-subgroup restriction semisimplicity; this is the generic group-theoretic tool.
Supplies the fixed nontrivial prime-field character for the local comparison.
Defines the boundary inertia map into the geometric fundamental group; the same-unit conventions give triviality of its action, but not the local map construction.

The item statement is the main-20261015 statement word for word; the explicit nontrivial psi is not a weakening, since every nontrivial psi is Psi(Tr(b.)) and a->ba is a bijection of k. Step 1: U is connected and U0 is geometrically connected, so the Weil representation is defined and the exact sequence makes G normal; rem-dl-a1-conventions gives that V is an irreducible W-module. Step 2: normal-restriction semisimplicity needs no finiteness of W/G (here Z), and Jordan-Holder factors of a semisimple module are summands. Step 3: k1 is finite containing k0(a); the comparison applies with X=A^1_{k1} and f=ax and gives exactly the sheaf e_Psi pi_* of u^p-u-bax from the ramification lemma, with ba in k1^x; I_infinity acts through a character of exact order p. Step 4: d-real-boundary applies to U0 in P^1_{k0}; unramified means I_infinity acts trivially (via rem-dl-a1-conventions and lem-dl-a1-lisse-extension-inertia); the equivariant injection gives the contradiction, and inertia factors through pi1(A^1_k). Step 5: the invariant-vector argument is genuinely elementary. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. New node: I verified T_b(y)=sum (by)^{p^i}, which gives T_b^p-T_b=b(y^q-y) and T_b(y+c)=T_b(y)+Tr(bc), and the character classification by nondegenerate trace. It holds for r=1, f=0 and p|r. It is statement-only, self-contained and searched, and a grep of the DAG finds no duplicate: lem-fd-as-cover and lem-fd-as-characters are degree-p only. It is not a restated clause of the item, and it is needed because the current def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf is degree-q while the ramification lemma is degree-p. Neither assumption gives these, and neither is a step of the proof of the trace formula or of Poincare duality.
